market_data.note: regular session 09:15-15:30 IST; bar stamps are bucket START times

post_trade_analysis.headline: The day was lost on entries, not exits.
post_trade_analysis.not_one_trade_cleared_its_own_risk: For all 7 closed trades the best favourable move was smaller than the initial stop distance.
post_trade_analysis.perfect_exit_note: Selling the exact intraday high of all 7 positions yields +7,834 — that is the absolute ceiling any exit-timing change could reach.

exit_policy_sweep.method: poll grid swept across all 15 minute-offsets x {closed-15m-bar price, live tick}
exit_policy_sweep.conclusion: The live-tick change has a small real positive edge, but it is SMALLER than the noise from which minute you happen to poll. On this day the schedule offset was luck, not improvement.

dominant_defect.name: trailing-stop compression
dominant_defect.detail: Stops are trailed to a fraction of a percent from entry, guaranteeing noise stop-outs.
dominant_defect.worst_case: BALKRISIND stop went 3.84% -> 1.79% -> 0.17% from entry in 36 minutes, was noise-stopped at 13:05, then rallied to +3.20% by the close. It would have been the day's best trade (+5,215 at its high).
dominant_defect.interaction_with_live_tick: Reacting to the live tick reaches a hair-thin stop SOONER, so the live-price fix amplifies this bug (BALKRISIND -1,325 -> -1,635). Fix stop compression first.

bug_pngsreva.detail: The stop was placed ABOVE both entry and target for a LONG while the tape was ~438. Every price below 452.10 satisfies 'ltp <= stop', so the exit was guaranteed the instant it was set. A trailing stop must never be set above the market for a long.

questions_for_the_skill: All 7 longs were entered into moves that immediately reversed — MFE < initial risk on every one. What entry filter would have rejected them?
3 of 7 (MOIL, BLACKBUCK, PNGSREVA) never traded green at all after entry — is the engine chasing extended moves rather than waiting for a pullback?
Initial stops averaged ~3.7% while the best favourable move averaged ~+0.6%. Is the R:R being computed against a target the tape never supports?
BALKRISIND was the one trade that worked (+3.2% by the close) and the trail stopped it out at +0.17%. Should the trail have a floor tied to ATR or to the initial risk?
